function: p. 1, 4-6: Over-the-air federated aggregation: each ED sends L random-projection scalars of its model update, superposed over the air with uniform-forcing receive beamforming; PS reconstructs the global update.
system: p. 3, 10: Uplink multi-user SIMO, K single-antenna EDs (20-160, 10 per round) and 8-antenna PS; analog OtA uplink, digital downlink broadcast; 2.4 GHz; no RIS.
method: p. 4-7, 10: Fed-ZOE: FedAvg local SGD, model-update compression by random projection (SRHT) with randomized gradient estimation, analog over-the-air aggregation; ResNet-18 trained federated on non-IID Dirichlet data.
data_channel: p. 10: 3GPP TR 38.901 UMi O2I channels at 2.4 GHz for the wireless links; learning data CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, Brain-CT, Tiny-ImageNet with Dirichlet partition (alpha 0.1, 0.5, 10).
test_conditions: p. 10-14: Trained for 70-300 rounds, tested on each dataset's test split; sweeps over K, local steps, projection dimension L, non-IID alpha and datasets; one fixed 3GPP channel setup.
baselines: p. 10-11: Canonical uncompressed OtA-FL [6]; LoRA-OtA-FL (ranks 8, 16, 32); Fed-ZO zeroth-order OtA FL [15], [31], [50]; no heuristic or digital-FL baseline.
metrics: p. 11-14: Test accuracy versus rounds and versus total communication and computation load (seconds); uplink and downlink bits per round; projection wall-clock time; gradient cosine similarity under dropout.
complexity: p. 3, 7, 11: SRHT projection O(S log S) versus O(SL) Gaussian; beamforming solved in 0.7 ms; compression adds 0.04 s per round; 16,384 scalars versus 1.1e7 parameters.
openness: none; the supplementary-material DOI (p. 1) is cited only for appendices with proofs and the beamforming solution (pp. 5-9); no code or data link.
q1_support: p. 10: "follow the 3GPP TR 38.901 Urban Micro (UMi) outdoor-to-indoor (O2I) model" at 2.4 GHz.
q2_support: p. 13: "we train ResNet-18 models via Fed-ZOE for various L" and non-IID levels, and K in {20, 80, 160} in Fig. 9, so each condition is a separate training run. Missing: no model trained under one setting is tested under another channel, K or dataset.
q3_support: p. 10: "OtA-FL: [6] A foundational method that uses the FedAvg algorithm with over-the-air aggregation." Also p. 11 "Fed-ZO: [15], [31], [50]" and "LoRA-OtA-FL: [33]", earlier designs compared on test accuracy and load (Figs. 5, 8, 9).
q4_support: p. 3: "reduces this cost to O(S log S)" for the SRHT projection, and p. 11: "which is generally done in 0.7 ms" for the beamformer; Fig. 2(a) gives wall-clock times.
q5_support: p. 1: "supplementary downloadable material available at https://doi.org/10.1109/JSAC.2026.3739217", which p. 8 describes as "Appendix B of the supplementary material" for proofs. No code or data link; CIFAR-10 and the other image sets are learning-task datasets.
notes: Area 7: the problem is communication-efficient over-the-air aggregation, with analog uplink aggregation (p. 11) and uniform-forcing combiner design (p. 5), and the PS has 8 antennas, so the system exclusion does not apply. q3 is borderline and flagged: every baseline trains the same ResNet-18; the non-learned side is the canonical uncompressed OtA-FL and the earlier-design side is Fed-ZO and LoRA-OtA-FL, with no random or greedy heuristic. The supplementary material is not part of the PDF and was not read; the text cites it only for appendices A-E.
